wins.text: FEC revenue grew 10% YoY with adjusted operating income up 18% ($252M), marking the sixth consecutive quarter of margin expansion (+50 bps)
Consolidated Q3 revenue up 8% YoY; December delivered the best monthly revenue performance in company history
FY'26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to $19.30–$20.10 from prior $17.80–$19.00, a midpoint increase of ~$1.30
FY'26 CapEx reduced to no more than $4.1B, down at least $400M from the prior $4.5B forecast, supporting upside to $3.8B adjusted free cash flow target
Transformation savings expected to exceed $1B target for FY'26; $2B cumulative savings from Network 2.0 and One FedEx initiatives on track by end of 2027

risks.text: MD-11 fleet grounding created a $120M adjusted operating income headwind in Q3, with an additional up to $55M headwind expected in Q4 as aircraft begin returning to service late in the quarter

FedEx Freight adjusted operating income declined $127M YoY; shipments down 6%, revenue down 5%, with ~$60M in separation-related costs not adjusted out; full-year freight AOI headwind now expected at $400M vs. prior $300M
Iran/Middle East conflict creating network disruption and a modest profit headwind in Q4; ~20% of air cargo capacity temporarily removed from market at peak of conflict
Global trade policy changes (transpacific capacity cut ~15–25%) and de minimis rule changes creating ongoing revenue and profit headwinds, partially offset by transformation savings
Q4 faces ~$0.10 EPS headwind from higher share count (~242M shares) due to no incremental buybacks and higher interest costs from FedEx Freight's $3.7B debt issuance

guidance_items.detail: FY'26 adjusted diluted EPS raised to $19.30–$20.10 from prior $17.80–$19.00; Q4 midpoint implies ~$5.80 adjusted EPS
FY'26 consolidated revenue growth now expected at 6%–6.5% vs. prior 5%–6%; Q4 consolidated revenue growth guided to 6%–7.5%
FEC full-year revenue growth midpoint now implies ~8% YoY; Q4 FEC revenue growth guided at ~8% at midpoint
FedEx Freight FY'26 revenue now expected down low single digits YoY; Q4 revenue flat to down slightly
FY'26 CapEx now expected no more than $4.1B, down at least $400M from prior $4.5B forecast

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Sustainability of simultaneous volume and yield growth — analysts questioned whether this is repeatable and how it compares to the broader freight market
Amazon volume onboarding contribution to ground/home delivery growth — management had not proactively quantified or named Amazon in prepared remarks
FedEx Freight margin trajectory at a 5-year low and whether top-line weakness is company-specific vs. purely macro-driven
